messages:
Maya: Quick q — can we move our canary fallback from single-threshold rules to a small 'signal orchestration' layer? idea: aggregator that votes across latency, error-rate, and quality-signal feeds before deciding an automatic fallback.
Liam: curious about latency here. grouping signals sounds safer but could delay failure action. what's our target decision SLO for a fail-open vs fail-closed?
Maya: agreed, we should split: a fast-path for safety-critical signals (5xx surge, infra OOMs) with <5s reaction, and a slow-path for quality regressions that uses an aggregation window (30s–2m) and can be revoked.
Serena: runtime note — KV cache + batching means a decision can be costly to roll back if sessions are warmed. need to factor session-eviction cost into the rollback policy. also quantized models have different warmup curves.
Dinesh: ops perspective: prefer deterministic, auditable decisions. if orchestration is voting-based, each input signal must include provenance + sampling rate. otherwise on-call will chase ghosts.
Carla: from product UX, automatic fallback needs a visible, immediate signal in Console + a short, editable explanation so PMs/SEs know why traffic shifted. also want a reversible operator override with a 10min grace window.
Maya: rough policy sketch:
```
policy: {
  fast_path: { triggers: [5xx_rate>2% | infra_degraded], action: fallback_immediate },
  slow_path: { signals: [latency_p95, qual_regression_score, error_trend], window: 60s, vote_threshold: 0.7, action: fallback_gradual }
}
```
Liam: vote_threshold semantics? weighted votes or simple majority? I think weighted by signal reliability (e.g., canary evals get more weight than sampled user telemetry).
Dinesh: weight makes sense but increases complexity. if we go weighted, require a default weight map and a clear audit trail of the math per decision. ops-bot: recorded_decision: id=dec-20260321-01, path=slow_path, inputs=[latency_p95:0.82, qual_regression:0.6, error_trend:0.1], score=0.71.
Serena: implementational constraint — runtime needs a non-blocking API to query 'should_fallback(model, tenant)' that returns (decision, reason_code, ttl). keep it cheap: use cached recent evaluation and only recompute on signal changes.
Carla: how do we handle dual-variant A/B experiments? product will want to continue collecting quality telemetry even after fallback. fallback shouldn't kill eval logging.
Maya: yes — fallback action = routing policy change (reduce variant share) + preserve telemetry lane. fallback modes: soft-reduce (from 20%->2%) or hard-cut (0%). soft-reduce preferred for quality signals.
Liam: rollout idea — start with orchestration in dry-run mode, emitting decisions and Console annotations but not flipping traffic. run for 2 weeks across low-traffic namespaces.
Dinesh: add safety nets: operator kill-switch, auto-revert after N minutes if fallback reduces throughput below SLA, and a circuit inspector endpoint that returns last 10 decisions.
Serena: perf note — voting aggregator should support incremental aggregates so we recompute in O(k) not O(n). and make evaluation idempotent.
Carla: deliverable asks: (1) RFC for policy DSL + weights, (2) Console UX mock for operator override + decision timeline, (3) dry-run telemetry dashboard. owner: Maya.
Maya: i'll draft RFC and include a simple reference impl (python prototype + grpc shim) for the runtime API. tagging folks: @Liam @Serena @Dinesh for review.
Liam: +1 on RFC. add a testplan with chaos runs where we induce a 5xx spike vs a slow quality drift.
Dinesh: +1. also include log retention for decision traces (30d) and an alert rule for 'orchestration_health'.
ops-bot: noted: created rfc/4759871234-signal-orch-draft in google-drive, assigned Maya, due 2026-04-04. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks — will share draft by EOD tomorrow and open a dry-run env.
Carla: sounds good.
Serena: thanks, leaving comments on the proto when you post it.
Liam: happy path + failure path test cases when ready.
